biomarker: femorotibial cartilage T2 (multi-echo spin echo T2 mapping of the weight-bearing femoral and tibial cartilage, 3 T), in ms

inputs.pilot_test_retest.csv: 22 healthy volunteers (V01..V22) scanned in two sessions 6 days apart; one row per participant, session and knee (L, R); columns subject_id, session, knee, cartilage_t2_ms, qc_pass
inputs.pilot_groups.csv: 18 patients with early knee osteoarthritis (OA01..OA18) and 15 asymptomatic controls (CT01..CT15) scanned once; one row per participant and knee; columns subject_id, group (early_oa or control), knee, cartilage_t2_ms, qc_pass
inputs.note: Pilot data are simulated for this evaluation.

endpoint: For one participant and session, the study endpoint is the mean of the left- and right-knee cartilage T2 values (ms).
qc_rule: Exclude every row with qc_pass = false. A test-retest participant without two sessions that pass QC is excluded from the repeatability analysis; a group-pilot participant whose scan fails QC is excluded from the group analysis.

estimands.within_subject_sd: square root of the within-participant mean square of the endpoint over the two sessions (one-way random-effects ANOVA with participant as the factor), with a 95% CI from the chi-square distribution on its degrees of freedom
estimands.icc: ICC(2,1) of the endpoint (Shrout and Fleiss: two-way random effects, absolute agreement, single measurement, sessions as the second factor) with its 95% CI from the Shrout and Fleiss / McGraw and Wong F-based interval
estimands.pilot_group_difference: mean endpoint difference, early_oa minus controls, with a 95% CI from the pooled-variance two-sample t interval, and the pooled within-group SD of the endpoint

acute_challenge.question: Does a standardized 30-minute treadmill run, finished 45 minutes before the scan, change the endpoint compared with a non-loading rest day in healthy volunteers?
acute_challenge.logistics: Volunteers comparable to the test-retest pilot. Each participant can be scanned on two days at least 5 days apart (after the run or after rest, in random order). The loading effect is acute and fully reversible; no carryover or period effect is expected. Assume that the day-to-day within-participant variability equals that of the test-retest pilot.

group_difference.question: Does the endpoint differ between patients with early knee osteoarthritis and asymptomatic controls?
group_difference.logistics: Cross-sectional, one scan per participant, equal group sizes. Use the variability observed in the group pilot.

sample_size_rules: For each study choose the most efficient valid design and the SD that matches it. Compute the number of evaluable units with the normal-approximation formula, rounding up: paired, n = ((z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta}) * SD / Delta)^2 where SD is the SD of the within-participant differences; independent groups, n per group = 2 * ((z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta}) * SD / Delta)^2. The exact noncentral-t calculation is also accepted. Then inflate for non-evaluable participants: n_enrol = ceil(n_evaluable / (1 - nonevaluable_fraction)).

design_json_schema.qc_exclusions: {test_retest: [subject_id..], groups: [subject_id..]} participants excluded by the QC rule
design_json_schema.repeatability: {n_participants, within_subject_sd, within_subject_sd_ci95: [lo, hi], repeatability_coefficient, icc_form: string, icc, icc_ci95: [lo, hi]}

designs.acute_challenge: {design, unit_of_analysis, sd_type, sd_used, effect, alpha, power, n_evaluable (participants), n_enrol (participants), rationale: string}
designs.group_difference: {design, unit_of_analysis, sd_type, sd_used, effect, alpha, power, n_evaluable_per_group, n_enrol_per_group, rationale: string}

plan_md_requirements: A short study plan of at most 1000 words.
State the chosen design, the SD used and the numbers to enrol for both studies, matching design.json.
grading_note: Deterministic automated checks: QC exclusions and counts, unit of analysis, within-subject SD and CI, repeatability coefficient, ICC and CI, pilot group estimates, design and SD choices, sample sizes (normal-approximation to exact-t range around the correct SD) and enrolment inflation, and plan.md consistency. Tolerances: within-subject SD and pooled SD 3%, their CI bounds 5%, ICC 0.01 and its CI bounds 0.02, mean difference 0.05 ms and CI bounds 0.1 ms, SD used in a design 4%. Deliverables are read from the workspace root or one subfolder.
